couplets.gloss: As the ground goes on holding up the people cutting into it, the best thing you can do is put up with those who run you down.

edges.reason: Asks you to carry your detractors the way the ground carries those who dig it.
edges.quote: bear with those who scorn you

edges.reason: The earth holding up the very people who dig into it is the whole model of patience.
edges.quote: the earth holds up those who dig into it

couplets.sensitive: urges bearing insult and abuse

couplets.gloss: Always pardon the harm people do you, and better still, wipe it from your mind entirely.

edges.reason: Sets a higher step above bearing a wrong: not remembering it at all.
edges.quote: Forgetting it is better still

couplets.sensitive: urges always forgiving and forgetting harm

couplets.gloss: The emptiest kind of want is turning a guest away, and the toughest kind of strength is staying patient with foolish people.

edges.reason: Puts bearing with fools at the very top of all strength.
edges.quote: The greatest strength is to bear with fools

edges.reason: Turning a guest away is named the deepest form of being poor.
edges.quote: The deepest poverty is to turn a guest away

couplets.sensitive: Counsel to bear with others, as in the rest of the chapter.

couplets.gloss: If you want your standing as a person to stay whole, make patience towards everybody a lasting habit.

edges.reason: Keeping your integrity is made to depend on guarding your patience.
edges.quote: guard your patience and live by it

couplets.sensitive: urges forgiving everyone without exception

couplets.gloss: Sensible people think nothing of someone who hits back, but they hold on dearly to anyone who lets an injury pass.

edges.reason: People who pay back a wrong are counted as nothing at all.
edges.quote: Those who punish a wrong are counted as nothing

edges.reason: Whoever bears a wrong is treasured the way gold is kept.
edges.quote: Those who bear it are wrapped up and kept like gold

couplets.sensitive: praises forgiving those who do you harm

couplets.gloss: Getting your own back feels good for a single day, while the honour of having let it go lasts as long as the world.

edges.reason: Puts a hard limit on what payback is worth: one day's pleasure.
edges.quote: Those who punish have one day’s pleasure

edges.reason: Against that single day, the one who bears a wrong has renown to the end.
edges.quote: Those who bear it have renown until the end

edges.reason: Someone planning payback can set its one day of joy against a lasting good name.
edges.quote: one day’s pleasure

couplets.sensitive: urges forgiving rather than answering an injury

couplets.gloss: However badly someone has treated you, the better course is not to nurse the hurt and not to do wrong back.

edges.reason: Asks you to take the pain of even the worst wrong and still do no wrong back.
edges.quote: suffer the pain and do nothing unrighteous

edges.reason: The size of the wrong gives no licence to pay it back.
edges.quote: do nothing unrighteous

couplets.sensitive: urges bearing even great wrongs

couplets.gloss: When arrogant people do you harm, beat them by being the better person.

edges.reason: Turns an injury into a contest won by your own worth, not by paying it back.
edges.quote: Defeat by your own worth

couplets.sensitive: urges answering injury with nobility

couplets.gloss: People who can bear cruel words from those who go too far are purer even than monks who have given up everything.

edges.reason: Those who bear cruel words are set beside the renouncers for purity.
edges.quote: bear cruel words from the mouths of people who overstep

couplets.sensitive: praises enduring cruel words

couplets.gloss: People who go hungry as a discipline deserve admiration, but they rank behind anyone who can take being spoken ill of.

edges.reason: Even the hard discipline of fasting ranks behind bearing cruel words.
edges.quote: they come after those who endure the cruel words of others

couplets.sensitive: praises enduring slander above all

couplets.gloss: Make it a rule for your life to keep your heart free of resentment at what others have.

edges.reason: Envy is to be kept out of the heart, as a rule of conduct.
edges.quote: keep your heart free of envy

couplets.gloss: Nothing you could be given is worth more than a nature that holds no jealousy towards anyone.

edges.reason: Rates having no envy at all above any blessing a person could receive.
edges.quote: free of envy towards everyone, no great blessing equals it

couplets.gloss: A person who resents a neighbour's success instead of welcoming it has clearly given up on goodness and on their own gain.

edges.reason: Envying another’s prosperity shows a person who cares nothing for their own righteousness or prosperity.
edges.quote: envies another’s prosperity

couplets.gloss: Sensible people won't do wrong out of jealousy, because they know the trouble that wrongdoing brings on them.

edges.reason: Those who can see the harm hold back from doing wrong through envy.
edges.quote: do nothing unrighteous out of envy

couplets.gloss: Jealousy needs no outside help: even if no enemy ever touches you, it will bring you down all by itself.

edges.reason: The envious need no enemy, since their own envy finishes the work.
edges.quote: Even if their enemies fail, it brings them ruin

edges.reason: Tells anyone eaten up by another's success that the resentment is itself the punishment.
edges.quote: Envy alone is enough for the envious

couplets.gloss: Someone who can't stand seeing others given things will watch their own family go without food and clothes, and fall apart.

edges.reason: Grudging what others are given ends with one's own family unfed and unclothed.
edges.quote: grudges what others are given

couplets.gloss: Good fortune can't stand a jealous person: she walks out and hands them over to her sister, misery.

edges.reason: The goddess of fortune cannot stand to stay beside the envious.
edges.quote: cannot bear the envious

edges.reason: The goddess of fortune departs and shows the envious to her elder sister.
edges.quote: She shows them to her elder sister and goes

couplets.gloss: Jealousy is a villain that wipes out what you have and drags you down to hell.

edges.reason: Personifies envy as a sinner who destroys your wealth and sends you to an evil place.
edges.quote: That sinner called envy

couplets.gloss: When a jealous person does well or a fair-minded person falls on hard times, it is strange enough to make you stop and wonder.

edges.reason: The prosperity of a crooked heart is so out of order that it needs thinking about.
edges.quote: a crooked heart prospers

couplets.gloss: Nobody ever got ahead through jealousy, and nobody free of it ever lost their prosperity.

edges.reason: There is no case of envy raising anyone up.
edges.quote: No one has grown great through envy

edges.reason: Shows someone measuring themselves against others that resentment has never got anyone further.
edges.quote: No one has grown great through envy

couplets.gloss: If you drop all fairness and reach for what belongs to someone else, your household will collapse and your wrongs will pile up.

edges.reason: Coveting good wealth without fairness brings down your family and brings faults at once.
edges.quote: covet good wealth

couplets.gloss: People who would be ashamed to act unfairly won't do something disgraceful just to get their hands on a profit.

edges.reason: Refusing to covet goes hand in hand with refusing deeds that bring blame.
edges.quote: won’t covet a gain and do what brings blame

couplets.gloss: Those after a deeper happiness won't do wrong for the sake of small, passing pleasures.

edges.reason: Those with another joy in view do not covet small pleasures or do wrong to get them.
edges.quote: won’t covet a small pleasure

couplets.gloss: People who have their senses in hand and see clearly won't reach for what isn't theirs, even on the excuse that they have nothing.

edges.reason: Being in want is not accepted as an excuse for coveting.
edges.quote: don’t say “We have nothing” and covet

edges.reason: Mastery of the senses is named as what keeps such people clear of it.
edges.quote: conquered their senses

couplets.gloss: What use is a sharp, wide-ranging mind if greed can still drive it to do senseless things to people?

edges.reason: Coveting empties out the worth of even the subtlest mind.
edges.quote: What use is a fine, wide understanding if you covet

couplets.gloss: Even someone who has set out on a path of compassion will be ruined if they start eyeing others' money and scheming for it.

edges.reason: Hankering after wealth can destroy even a seeker already walking the path.
edges.quote: perish if they covet wealth and plot evil

couplets.gloss: Don't want riches that come from grabbing, because when the time comes to enjoy them they turn sour.

edges.reason: Warns that the gain from coveting will bear no good fruit when it ripens.
edges.quote: When it ripens, the fruit is hardly ever good

couplets.gloss: If you want your own wealth not to shrink, stop wanting what someone else has in hand.

edges.reason: Offers a plain bargain: leave another’s wealth alone and your own will hold.
edges.quote: Not coveting the wealth in another’s hands

couplets.gloss: Prosperity recognises the person who knows what is right and doesn't grasp at others' goods, and goes looking for them.

edges.reason: Knowing righteousness and not coveting is what draws fortune to you.
edges.quote: know righteousness and don’t covet

edges.reason: Fortune is pictured as knowing the way and coming to the wise.
edges.quote: Fortune knows the way

couplets.gloss: Thoughtless grabbing brings ruin, while the proud strength of wanting nothing wins out over everything.

edges.reason: Coveting that never looks ahead gives birth to destruction.
edges.quote: Coveting without thought breeds destruction

edges.reason: The pride of wanting nothing is said to breed victory.
edges.quote: The pride of wanting nothing breeds victory

couplets.gloss: Even someone who ignores morality and does wrong is glad to be known as a person who doesn't talk behind people's backs.

edges.reason: Not backbiting is so prized that it is good to be credited with it, even for one who does wrong.
edges.quote: it is good to have it said that they don’t backbite

couplets.gloss: Openly doing wrong is bad, but being all smiles to someone's face while tearing them down in their absence is far worse.

edges.reason: Ranks the smile in front and the smear behind below open wrongdoing.
edges.quote: ruin someone behind their back and smile falsely to their face

couplets.gloss: Better to die than stay alive by backstabbing and false smiles; death would bring the reward that virtue promises.

edges.reason: A life propped up by backbiting is rated lower than dying.
edges.quote: live by backbiting and lies

edges.reason: Lying is named alongside backbiting as a living not worth keeping.
edges.quote: Better to die than to live by backbiting and lies

couplets.sensitive: calls death better than a life of lies

couplets.gloss: Whatever harsh words pass face to face, never speak ill of someone behind their back.

edges.reason: Forbids backbiting outright, whatever has been said to one's face.
edges.quote: don’t speak when they aren’t there

couplets.sensitive: urges silence about one who insults you

couplets.gloss: You can tell someone's talk of goodness is hollow from the pettiness of what they say behind people's backs.
keywords: saying one thing and doing another

edges.reason: Backbiting gives away the small heart behind someone’s talk of righteousness.
edges.quote: the meanness of their backbiting

couplets.gloss: Spread someone's faults about and they will dig out yours and broadcast the most damaging ones.

edges.reason: Telling another’s faults invites having your own picked out and told.
edges.quote: will have their own picked out with care and told

couplets.gloss: People who can't keep friendships going with pleasant talk end up using divisive talk to turn friends against each other.

edges.reason: Talk that splits friends apart is the backbiter's work.
edges.quote: speak words that divide, and drive friends apart

edges.reason: Lacking the art of words that bring smiles is what turns a person into a splitter of friends.
edges.quote: make friends with words that bring smiles

couplets.gloss: If people make a habit of broadcasting the faults of those close to them, imagine what they will do to strangers.

edges.reason: One who spreads the faults of those close will spare no one else.
edges.quote: spread even the faults of those close to them

couplets.gloss: It's a wonder the world goes on carrying someone who waits for people to turn away before sneering at them; perhaps only out of duty.

edges.reason: The backbiter’s very weight is treated as something hard to bear.
edges.quote: the earth bears the weight of someone who waits for your back to speak mean words

edges.reason: The earth is pictured as bearing the backbiter’s weight only for righteousness’ sake.
edges.quote: the earth bears the weight

couplets.gloss: If people looked at their own faults the way they look at those of their enemies, what harm could ever reach them?

edges.reason: Asks for the same scrutiny of yourself that you gladly give a stranger.
edges.quote: see your own faults as you see strangers’ faults

couplets.gloss: Someone who irritates the whole room with pointless talk ends up looked down on by everyone.

edges.reason: Pointless talk that grates on the many earns the scorn of all.
edges.quote: speaks useless words, to the disgust of many, is scorned by all

couplets.gloss: Talking uselessly in front of a crowd does more harm than doing something unkind to your friends.

edges.reason: Worthless talk before many is ranked as worse than wronging a friend.
edges.quote: worse than doing unkind things to your friends

couplets.gloss: Going on and on about nothing announces to everyone that you have nothing to offer.

edges.reason: Spinning out useless talk is itself a notice that the speaker has no goodness.
edges.quote: the speaker has no goodness

couplets.gloss: Worthless talk in company gains you nothing and cuts you off from everything good.

edges.reason: Idle words in company drive every good thing from the speaker's side.
edges.quote: they take you away from all that is good

couplets.gloss: Even people of real merit lose their standing and respect once they start talking nonsense.

edges.reason: No stock of merit is safe once a person takes to idle talk.
edges.quote: their worth and the respect it brings will leave them

couplets.gloss: Someone who enjoys pointless talk shouldn't be called a person at all, only the useless husk of one.

edges.reason: Someone who keeps repeating useless words is denied the name of person and called chaff.
edges.quote: Call them chaff among people

couplets.gloss: Good people may say something harsh if they must, but they should keep well away from saying anything useless.

edges.reason: Words without goodness may sometimes be allowed, useless ones never.
edges.quote: It is good that they say nothing useless

couplets.gloss: People whose minds are on matters of real value don't bother saying things that carry no benefit.

edges.reason: A mind that seeks out rare gains leaves no room for words of little use.
edges.quote: won’t say words without great use

couplets.gloss: People who see clearly and aren't confused won't say anything meaningless, even by accident.

edges.reason: Clear sight holds back empty words even in an unguarded moment.
edges.quote: won’t say empty words even by a slip

edges.reason: Whole, healthy eyes stand for a mind free of confusion.
edges.quote: They whose eyes are whole

couplets.gloss: Say what is worth saying, and never say anything that does no one any good.

edges.reason: Gives the whole rule of talk in a line: say what profits, never what does not.
edges.quote: Of words, say the ones with use. Of words, don’t say the ones without

couplets.gloss: People set on wrongdoing aren't afraid of it, but the truly good dread that kind of arrogance.

edges.reason: Fearing evil deeds is what separates the worthy from those who do them.
edges.quote: don’t fear the arrogance called evil deeds. The worthy do

couplets.gloss: Bad deeds only give rise to more harm, so dread them even more than you would dread being burned.

edges.reason: Since evil only breeds more evil, it deserves more dread than the worst flame.
edges.quote: evil should be feared more than fire

edges.reason: Fire is the yardstick of danger, and evil goes past it.
edges.quote: feared more than fire

couplets.gloss: People say the highest kind of intelligence is refusing to do harm even to someone who hates you.

edges.reason: Sparing an enemy from harm is called the crown of all wisdom.
edges.quote: do no evil even to those who hate you

couplets.gloss: Don't plot someone's downfall even in a careless moment, because goodness itself will plot the downfall of the plotter.

edges.reason: Forbids planning another's ruin, even absent-mindedly.
edges.quote: Don’t plot another’s ruin, even in a moment of forgetting

couplets.gloss: Don't do wrong on the excuse that you are broke: it will only leave you worse off than before.

edges.reason: Poverty is no shelter: evil done in its name only makes you poor again.
edges.quote: Don’t do evil because you are poor

edges.reason: Answers the plea of being short of money: the wrong only brings the want back.
edges.quote: you will be poor again

couplets.gloss: If you don't want pain to crush you, don't do bad things to other people.

edges.reason: Whoever wants to stay clear of suffering must start by injuring no one.
edges.quote: don’t do evil things to others

couplets.gloss: You can get away from any other enemy, but the harm you have done never dies: it follows you and brings you down.

edges.reason: Evil deeds are the one enemy with no escape: they hunt down their doer.
edges.quote: The enemy that is your own deed never goes away

couplets.gloss: Just as your shadow goes everywhere with you, the harm you have done stays at your heels until it finishes you.

edges.reason: Ruin stays as close to those who do evil as a shadow stays at the feet.
edges.quote: like a shadow that never leaves

edges.reason: The shadow gives the reason for dread: a wrong done cannot be walked away from.
edges.quote: The ruin of those who do evil

couplets.gloss: If you care about yourself at all, don't go anywhere near wrongdoing, however small.
keywords: first step down a bad road

edges.reason: Turns self-love into an argument against the slightest lean towards evil.
edges.quote: If you love yourself, don’t go near evil deeds at all

couplets.gloss: Someone who won't step off the proper road to do wrong can be counted safe from ruin.

edges.reason: Refusing to turn aside to do evil is what keeps a person safe from ruin.
edges.quote: doesn’t stray aside to do evil

couplets.gloss: Real service to others wants nothing back: what does the world ever give the rain in return?

edges.reason: Duty done for others looks for nothing in return.
edges.quote: Duty asks for no return

edges.reason: Nobody repays the cloud, and that is the pattern for unpaid service.
edges.quote: What does the world give back to the rain?

edges.reason: Speaks to someone tired of getting nothing back: the rain never does either.
edges.quote: What does the world give back to the rain?

couplets.gloss: Everything good people earn through hard work is there so they can be of use to others.

edges.reason: All the wealth earned by effort is said to exist for helping the worthy.
edges.quote: is for helping the worthy

couplets.gloss: Neither on earth nor in heaven could you find anything finer than being of service to others.

edges.reason: Searches earth and heaven and finds nothing better.
edges.quote: hard to find anything better than helping others

couplets.gloss: Only someone who understands what they owe to the people around them is really alive; anyone else may as well be counted among the dead.

edges.reason: Knowing what is fitting towards others is made the mark of being alive.
edges.quote: Whoever knows what is fitting is alive

edges.reason: One with no sense of that duty is filed among the corpses while he breathes.
edges.quote: counted among the dead

couplets.sensitive: Classes people as good as dead.

couplets.gloss: The wealth of a wise person who cares about everyone is like a village pond full to the top, there for all.

edges.reason: Wealth in the hands of one who loves the world lies open to everyone.
edges.quote: The wealth of a person of great understanding who loves the world

edges.reason: The brimming tank, free to all who come, pictures shared prosperity.
edges.quote: the village tank filled with water

couplets.gloss: Money held by a kind person is like a fruit tree ripening in the centre of town, where anyone can reach it.

edges.reason: A good person’s wealth feeds the people around them.
edges.quote: When wealth falls to a good person

edges.reason: A tree fruiting mid-village is there for every passer-by.
edges.quote: a fruit tree ripening inside the village

couplets.gloss: Wealth with a big-hearted person is like a plant whose every part heals and that never fails those who need it.

edges.reason: In the keeping of a person of great worth, wealth goes on relieving need.
edges.quote: wealth falls to a person of great worth

edges.reason: A medicine tree that never fails pictures help that always remains.
edges.quote: a tree that serves as medicine and never fails

couplets.gloss: Those who see clearly what they owe don't stop helping others, even when they have little left themselves.

edges.reason: Even lean times do not release those who know their duty.
edges.quote: those who know their duty won’t slacken in helping others

couplets.gloss: For a person of goodwill, being poor only means not being able to do what others need of them.

edges.reason: Such a person is poor only on the day they cannot do what they must.
edges.quote: A good person’s poverty is this

couplets.gloss: Even if being helpful ruined you, that ruin would be worth buying at the price of selling yourself.

edges.reason: Holds that ruin brought on by helping is worth buying at any price.
edges.quote: that ruin is worth buying

couplets.sensitive: says ruining oneself for others is worth it

couplets.gloss: Real giving is giving to people who have nothing; any other gift is a kind of loan that expects something back.

edges.reason: Draws the line: only what goes to the poor counts, and the rest is lending.
edges.quote: Only giving to those who have nothing is giving

couplets.gloss: Taking is wrong even if it would get you to heaven, and giving is right even if no heaven awaited you.
keywords: doing good for its own sake

edges.reason: Giving stays a virtue even with heaven taken off the table.
edges.quote: Even if there were no higher world, giving is good

couplets.sensitive: calls receiving help a bad thing

couplets.gloss: Only a person of real breeding gives without first complaining that they have nothing to spare.
keywords: saying no to someone in need

edges.reason: True giving never hides behind the plea of having nothing.
edges.quote: Never speaking the misery of “I have nothing”, and giving

edges.reason: Tells the person being asked to give, with no talk of having nothing.
edges.quote: Never speaking the misery of “I have nothing”, and giving

couplets.sensitive: ties generosity to high birth

couplets.gloss: Being asked for help stays uncomfortable until you see the person who asked go away happy.

edges.reason: The giver's own gladness waits on the contented smile of the one who asked.
edges.quote: until you see the pleased face of the one who begged

edges.reason: Sets the measure for someone being asked: the matter is settled when the asker can smile.
edges.quote: until you see the pleased face of the one who begged

couplets.gloss: The strength to bear one's own hunger is great, but it ranks behind the strength of those who end other people's hunger.

edges.reason: Ending hunger outranks even the strength of bearing your own.
edges.quote: It comes after the strength of those who end that hunger

couplets.gloss: Feeding people who have nothing is where someone with money should keep their savings.

edges.reason: Ending the hunger of those with nothing is given as the proper use of wealth.
edges.quote: End the ruinous hunger of those who have nothing

edges.reason: Ending hunger is pictured as the place to store your wealth.
edges.quote: where someone who has wealth can store it

couplets.gloss: Someone who makes a habit of sharing their food will never be struck by the terrible sickness of hunger.

edges.reason: Sharing your food is what keeps hunger from ever reaching you.
edges.quote: someone used to sharing their food

edges.reason: Hunger is named as a wicked illness that cannot infect the sharer.
edges.quote: The evil disease called hunger

couplets.gloss: Do the cold-hearted who sit on their money until it is lost not know the pleasure of making someone glad by giving?

edges.reason: Hoarders lose their wealth anyway, by the very act of keeping it.
edges.quote: hoard what they own and lose it

edges.reason: Names giving as a delight the hoarder has somehow never tasted.
edges.quote: the joy of giving

edges.reason: Puts the question to someone sitting on unused wealth: have you never known this joy?
edges.quote: Do they not know the joy of giving

couplets.gloss: Eating alone what you have piled up for yourself is a more miserable thing than begging for your food.

edges.reason: Eating your hoard alone is made worse than begging.
edges.quote: eating alone what you have piled up

couplets.gloss: Dying is the worst thing there is, yet it would be welcome next to being unable to give to those in need.

edges.reason: Losing the power to give is painted as worse than the bitterest thing there is.
edges.quote: Even that is sweet when you can’t give

couplets.sensitive: calls death sweet when one cannot give

couplets.gloss: Give to those in need and live so that people speak well of you: nothing else is real gain in life.

edges.reason: Renown is declared the only gain a soul can have.
edges.quote: There is no other gain for the soul

edges.reason: Giving comes first, as the deed that earns renown.
edges.quote: Give, and live with renown

couplets.gloss: Everything that people say in praise comes down, in the end, to those who give to the needy.

edges.reason: All the world's praise comes to rest on a single renown.
edges.quote: All that speakers say is renown

edges.reason: Those who give to people who beg are named as the sole subject of all that is said.
edges.quote: those who give something to those who beg

couplets.gloss: Nothing in this world lasts except a great name left behind.

edges.reason: Of all things in the world, only unrivalled renown escapes death.
edges.quote: nothing in the world stands undying

couplets.gloss: Earn a lasting name across the world and heaven itself will value you above the learned.

edges.reason: The world of the gods puts the one with lasting renown ahead of the learned.
edges.quote: the world of the gods will no longer honour the learned

couplets.gloss: Losses that only raise a person's standing, and a death that makes their name live, are for the rare and gifted few.

edges.reason: Only the skilled can turn ruin and death into renown.
edges.quote: A ruin that is gain, a death that is life

couplets.sensitive: glorifies ruin and death

couplets.gloss: If you're going to appear in the world, do it with distinction; for those without it, not appearing would have been better.

edges.reason: Ranks a life without renown lower than never having appeared.
edges.quote: appear with renown

couplets.sensitive: says the undistinguished should not have been born

couplets.gloss: People who fail to earn a good name should blame themselves, so why get angry at those who look down on them?

edges.reason: Turns the anger felt at one's critics back on the faults that gave them their chance.
edges.quote: should blame themselves

couplets.sensitive: tells the reviled to blame themselves

couplets.gloss: Everyone agrees that leaving no good name behind is a shame for any person on earth.

edges.reason: Leaving no remembered name behind is called a disgrace for anyone.
edges.quote: not to gain the legacy called renown

couplets.gloss: A land that has to carry people of no distinction loses even the rich yield it was always known for.

edges.reason: Even a land’s rich yield shrinks under a body with no renown.
edges.quote: a body without renown

edges.reason: The ground is shown losing its yield under the weight of those it carries.
edges.quote: Land that carries a body without renown

couplets.gloss: Only those free of reproach are truly living; those who live without a good name are not living at all.

edges.reason: Makes a good name the test of whether a life counts as a life.
edges.quote: Only those who live free of disgrace are alive

edges.reason: Those who go on breathing without renown are the ones counted as dead.
edges.quote: Those who live without renown are not alive

couplets.sensitive: Says those without glory are as good as dead.

couplets.gloss: The best kind of riches is a compassionate heart, since plain money can end up with even the worst people.

edges.reason: Compassion is valued above goods, which even the low can have.
edges.quote: The wealth of compassion is the wealth among wealth

edges.reason: Compassion takes the title of chief wealth from anything merely material.
edges.quote: The wealth of compassion

couplets.gloss: Look carefully and practise compassion: however many paths you examine, it is the one thing that will see you through.

edges.reason: However many ways you test it, compassion remains the one support.
edges.quote: it is still your only support

couplets.gloss: People whose hearts are filled with compassion will never have to enter the black world of suffering.

edges.reason: A heart full of compassion is spared the world of pain.
edges.quote: hearts are full of compassion

edges.reason: The place of punishment is pictured as a world without light.
edges.quote: the dark, painful world

couplets.gloss: They say someone who protects all living things out of compassion has no dreadful consequences to fear for themselves.

edges.reason: Tending living beings shields a person from deeds their own soul fears.
edges.quote: tend living beings and hold to compassion

couplets.gloss: Compassionate people don't come to real misery, and the whole wide living world is there to prove it.

edges.reason: Calls the whole earth as witness that misery does not touch the compassionate.
edges.quote: Those who hold to compassion have no misery

couplets.gloss: Those who drop compassion and live by doing harm are people, it is said, who have lost sight of what life is for.

edges.reason: Abandoning compassion to do wrong is called forgetting what truly matters.
edges.quote: leave compassion and go on doing wrong

couplets.gloss: Just as life here is closed to those with no money, the next life is closed to those with no compassion.

edges.reason: Without compassion the next world is shut, as this one is to those without wealth.
edges.quote: That world is not for those without compassion

couplets.sensitive: says this world is not for the poor

couplets.gloss: People short of money may recover some day, but those short of compassion are finished for good.

edges.reason: A lack of wealth can be made good, but a lack of compassion hardly ever can.
edges.quote: Those who lose compassion are lost

edges.reason: Sets the loss of compassion against the loss of wealth and finds only the first incurable.
edges.quote: Those who lose wealth may flower again one day. Those who lose compassion are lost

couplets.gloss: If you look closely, good deeds from someone without compassion are as unlikely as a muddled person grasping the deepest truth.

edges.reason: Righteousness without compassion is no surer than a confused mind glimpsing the truth.
edges.quote: the righteousness done by someone without compassion

couplets.gloss: When you are about to go after someone weaker, picture yourself shaking in front of someone stronger than you.

edges.reason: Checks the impulse to oppress by imagining oneself the one who trembles.
edges.quote: go against those weaker than you

edges.reason: Gives anyone with power a test: imagine standing before someone stronger.
edges.quote: think of yourself before those stronger

couplets.gloss: How can someone who eats another creature's body to bulk up their own have any real compassion?

edges.reason: Fattening your own flesh on another’s rules out any claim to compassion.
edges.quote: eats other flesh to swell their own

couplets.gloss: Just as money won't stay with people who don't look after it, compassion won't stay with people who eat flesh.

edges.reason: As the careless cannot keep wealth, the eater of flesh cannot keep compassion.
edges.quote: those who eat flesh don’t get to hold compassion

couplets.gloss: Like the mind of someone carrying a weapon, the mind of someone enjoying an animal's body isn't drawn to kindness.

edges.reason: Tasting flesh is said to turn the heart away from good.
edges.quote: the mind of one who has tasted a creature’s body doesn’t turn to good

edges.reason: Someone gripping a weapon is the comparison for a heart closed to good.
edges.quote: the heart of someone holding a weapon

couplets.gloss: Killing is what having no compassion looks like, and eating what was killed is a wrong as well.

edges.reason: Killing is named as the very opposite of compassion.
edges.quote: What is compassion? Not killing. What is not? Killing

edges.reason: Eating the flesh is counted a wrong of its own beyond the killing.
edges.quote: Eating that flesh is worthless

couplets.gloss: Life itself depends on not eating flesh: eat it and hell will never let you go.

edges.reason: Hell's mouth stays shut on the eater of flesh, while life lies in refusing it.
edges.quote: Life endures in not eating flesh

couplets.gloss: If people stopped killing for food, no one would be selling meat: demand is what keeps the trade going.

edges.reason: Lays the butcher's business at the door of the people who want to eat.
edges.quote: no one would offer flesh for money

edges.reason: Tells someone uneasy about meat that buying it is what keeps it on sale.
edges.quote: If the world didn’t kill in order to eat

couplets.gloss: Anyone who truly felt that meat is another creature's wound would not want to eat it.

edges.reason: Knowing flesh for a wound is enough to end the wish to eat it.
edges.quote: Flesh is another creature’s wound

edges.reason: Asks the doubtful eater to see flesh as another creature’s wound and then decide.
edges.quote: If you know that, you must not eat it

couplets.gloss: People whose vision is clear of error won't eat a body that life has left.

edges.reason: Freedom from fault shows itself in refusing flesh parted from life.
edges.quote: won’t eat flesh that has parted from life

couplets.gloss: Not killing a creature and eating it is worth more than a thousand fire offerings.

edges.reason: One refusal to eat a slain creature outweighs a thousand offerings.
edges.quote: not to take one creature’s life and eat it

edges.reason: Sparing a creature's life ranks above the whole apparatus of ritual.
edges.quote: Better than pouring offerings into a thousand sacrifices is not to take one creature’s life

couplets.gloss: All living beings press their palms together in respect for the person who won't kill or eat meat.

edges.reason: All living beings join hands in reverence to one who refuses flesh.
edges.quote: join their hands and worship one who doesn’t kill and refuses flesh

edges.reason: Not killing is the first half of what wins that universal honour.
edges.quote: one who doesn’t kill

couplets.gloss: Spiritual discipline comes down to two things: bearing your own pain and causing no pain to any living being.

edges.reason: Reduces the whole of austerity to bearing pain and causing no pain.
edges.quote: that is the form of austerity

edges.reason: Not hurting any living thing is half of what austerity is said to be.
edges.quote: cause no pain to any living being

couplets.sensitive: makes enduring suffering the whole of discipline

couplets.gloss: Spiritual practice only works for those already suited to it; for anyone else, taking it on is pointless.

edges.reason: Sets the test of austerity: those without it gain nothing by taking it up.
edges.quote: taking it up is in vain

couplets.gloss: Have all the others given up on discipline just so someone is left to look after those who renounced the world?

edges.reason: Teases everyone else for dropping austerity as if providing for renouncers excused them.
edges.quote: Have the others forgotten austerity

couplets.gloss: Think it through and you will see that the power to bring down enemies and lift up friends comes through spiritual discipline.

edges.reason: Claims for austerity the power to crush enemies and raise those who are dear.
edges.quote: austerity can do both

couplets.gloss: People take up spiritual discipline here because it gets them whatever they want, just the way they want it.

edges.reason: Gives the reason people strive at austerity: it grants every wish exactly as wished.
edges.quote: what you want comes as you want it

couplets.gloss: People who practise discipline are doing their real work; everyone else is tangled in wanting and just wasting themselves.

edges.reason: Only those doing austerity are said to be truly minding their own work.
edges.quote: Those who do austerity do their own work

edges.reason: Everyone else is caught in craving, doing what comes to nothing.
edges.quote: caught in craving

couplets.gloss: As gold glows brighter the hotter it is heated, those who hold to discipline shine purer the more they go through.

edges.reason: Harder suffering only refines the nature of the austere.
edges.quote: shine brighter the more pain burns them

edges.reason: The refiner's flame that brightens gold pictures hardship that purifies.
edges.quote: gold that shines brighter the more it is burned

couplets.sensitive: says suffering purifies the sufferer

couplets.gloss: The person who has fully taken charge of their own self is honoured by every other living being.

edges.reason: All other beings worship the one who has wholly won their own soul.
edges.quote: wholly won their own soul

couplets.gloss: People who have gained strength through discipline can get past even death itself.

edges.reason: The strength won by austerities is said to reach as far as defeating death.
edges.quote: can even leap past death

couplets.gloss: The world has so many people in need because only a few practise discipline and most do not.

edges.reason: Explains the world’s want by how few take up austerity.
edges.quote: few do austerity and many don’t

couplets.sensitive: blames poverty on lack of discipline

couplets.gloss: The very elements inside a deceitful person's body laugh to themselves at the show of virtue.

edges.reason: The hypocrite can fool others, but the stuff of his own body sees through him and laughs.
edges.quote: laugh to themselves at the hidden conduct

couplets.gloss: What good is a lofty, holy appearance if you know in your own heart that you are guilty?

edges.reason: A towering exterior does nothing for a heart that knows its own evil.
edges.quote: a look as high as the sky

couplets.gloss: A person with no inner strength dressing up as a formidable holy man is just a cow under a tiger's hide.

edges.reason: Someone with no strength looks fierce but is only a cow inside a tiger’s skin.
edges.quote: a cow wearing a tiger’s skin

couplets.gloss: Doing wrong from behind a show of holiness is like a bird-catcher lying in wait in a bush.

edges.reason: Austerity is a hunter’s bush, cover from which to do wrong.
edges.quote: hide behind austerity and do wrong

couplets.gloss: Those who claim to be free of desire while living a lie end up in trouble, crying out in regret at what they did.

edges.reason: The boast of having no attachments ends in the cry of “What have we done?”
edges.quote: until they cry “What have we done?”

couplets.gloss: No one is crueller than a person who hasn't given anything up inwardly but lives off people by acting as if they had.

edges.reason: Playing the renouncer to cheat people is ranked the hardest-hearted thing of all.
edges.quote: live by deceit, as if they had renounced

couplets.gloss: Some people look bright and clean from the outside, like the red seed, but inside they are as black as its tip.

edges.reason: The two-coloured crab’s-eye seed stands for people red outside and black within.
edges.quote: red outside like the crab’s-eye seed, yet black inside

couplets.gloss: Plenty of people with dirty minds take ritual baths to look holy and go around concealing what they really are.

edges.reason: Bathing to look worthy leaves the stain in the mind as it was.
edges.quote: the stain still in their minds

couplets.gloss: An arrow is straight yet deadly and a lute is bent yet sweet, so go by what people do, not how they look.

edges.reason: Lays down the rule for sizing up anyone: by what they do, not how they appear.
edges.quote: Judge people the same way, by what they do

edges.reason: The arrow's straight shape tells nothing of what it does.
edges.quote: An arrow is cruel

edges.reason: Someone weighing up a new person should go by their record, not their manner.
edges.quote: Judge people the same way, by what they do

couplets.gloss: You don't need a shaved head or long matted hair to be holy, as long as you keep away from what the world rightly condemns.

edges.reason: Simply shunning what the world condemns makes every outward mark of holiness needless.
edges.quote: give up what the world condemns

couplets.gloss: If you don't want people to despise you, keep your mind clear of any thought of cheating anyone.

edges.reason: Escaping contempt means guarding the heart against stealing.
edges.quote: guard their heart from stealing anything at all

couplets.gloss: Even quietly planning to get something from someone by a trick is already a wrong.

edges.reason: The evil begins with merely thinking, “We will steal.”
edges.quote: Even to think it in your mind is evil

couplets.gloss: Wealth made by cheating can look like it is growing without limit, but it is already on its way to vanishing.

edges.reason: Gain from stealing only seems to grow before it perishes.
edges.quote: Gain won by stealing seems to grow

edges.reason: Warns anyone eyeing a dishonest profit that its early growth is no proof it will last.
edges.quote: Gain won by stealing seems to grow, then perishes

couplets.gloss: An obsession with taking what isn't yours, once it ripens, brings pain that never ends.

edges.reason: The love of stealing has its harvest, and the crop is unending grief.
edges.quote: brings grief that never dies

couplets.gloss: Someone watching for a chance to catch people off guard and take their things has no room in them for mercy or love.

edges.reason: Waiting for others to slip leaves no place for compassion or loving-kindness.
edges.quote: watch for others to slip

edges.reason: Wanting what others hold is where this ambush begins.
edges.quote: want wealth and watch for others to slip

couplets.gloss: People hooked on taking what isn't theirs can't stay within proper limits or keep to what is right.

edges.reason: A hardened love of stealing bars a person from living within measure.
edges.quote: can’t live within measure

couplets.gloss: The dark cleverness of cheating isn't found in someone who has built up the strength of knowing the proper limit.

edges.reason: The dark understanding called stealing has no place in those who hold to measure.
edges.quote: The dark understanding called stealing

couplets.gloss: Just as goodness lives in the mind of someone who knows proper limits, trickery lives in the mind of someone who knows stealing.

edges.reason: Deceit settles in the thief’s heart as surely as righteousness in the hearts of those who know measure.
edges.quote: deceit stands in the hearts of those who know stealing

couplets.gloss: Those who can think of nothing but stealing do things beyond all limits and are destroyed by them.

edges.reason: A mind given over to theft walks itself off the right path and dies of it.
edges.quote: Those who know nothing but stealing

couplets.gloss: Cheats lose their grip even on their own bodies, while heaven never slips away from those who don't cheat.

edges.reason: The thief loses hold even of the body, while those who don’t steal keep the world of the gods.
edges.quote: For those who steal, the body itself will fail

ideaLinks.reason: Sets the one day’s pleasure of punishing against the lasting renown of bearing a wrong.
ideaLinks.quote: Those who punish have one day’s pleasure. Those who bear it have renown until the end

ideaLinks.reason: The one who bears a wrong is promised renown that lasts.
ideaLinks.quote: Those who bear it have renown until the end

ideaLinks.reason: Envy itself is named as what destroys your wealth.
Coveting breeds destruction while the pride of wanting nothing breeds victory.
ideaLinks.quote: Coveting without thought breeds destruction. The pride of wanting nothing breeds victory

ideaLinks.reason: Deeds the soul fears do not belong to one who tends living beings with compassion.
ideaLinks.quote: have no deeds that make their own soul afraid

ideaLinks.reason: Compassion cannot be held by one who eats flesh, any more than wealth by one who doesn’t guard it.
ideaLinks.quote: those who eat flesh don’t get to hold compassion

ideaLinks.reason: Causing no pain is one of the two things that make up the whole of austerity.
ideaLinks.quote: cause no pain to any living being

ideaLinks.reason: Those who do austerity serve their own good while the rest are caught in craving.
ideaLinks.quote: Those who do austerity do their own work. The rest are caught in craving

ideaLinks.reason: A hardened love of stealing ripens in time into grief without end.
ideaLinks.quote: A hardened love of stealing, when it ripens, brings grief that never dies
